answer: Each identity stakes one quartz vein segment on a ridge and files its claim pegs with the fable register, locking a 95-credit bond. A ridge auditor checks peg coordinates against the register: a claim overlapping an earlier claim, reusing pegs, or carrying a mismatched key forfeits the bond. Fees climb with order: the k-th claim pays 29+8(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th pays 8,021 and 1,000 fakes cost 4,025,000 in fees plus 95,000 locked. A rented-peg ring fails: pegs bind to one key and one segment and cannot be refiled. An honest staker spends 29 once and gets the 95 back after a clean epoch.
